items.followUp: State two limitations of Bohr’s atomic model.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for identifying the failure to explain atomic stability.
rubric.description: Rutherford’s model could not explain why electrons do not lose energy and fall into the nucleus.
rubric.how: Explain that orbiting electrons should lose energy and fall into the nucleus, but atoms remain stable.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for identifying another limitation of the model.
rubric.description: The model could not explain the line spectra emitted by atoms.
rubric.how: State that Rutherford’s model could not explain the discrete line spectra of atoms.

modelAnswer: Rutherford’s model could not explain the stability of the atom: orbiting electrons should lose energy and fall into the nucleus.
It also could not explain the line spectra emitted by atoms.

items.followUp: What was the main aim of alchemists?

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for describing alchemy as an early practice related to chemistry.
rubric.description: Alchemy was an early practice or branch related to chemistry.
rubric.how: Identify alchemy as an early practice related to chemistry.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for giving a characteristic aim of alchemists.
rubric.description: Alchemists tried to convert base metals into gold or searched for an elixir of life.
rubric.how: Mention the attempt to make gold from base metals or the search for an elixir of life.

modelAnswer: Alchemy was an early practice related to chemistry.
Alchemists tried to convert base metals into gold and searched for an elixir of life.

items.followUp: Write two properties of polar covalent compounds.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for stating the generally low melting or boiling points of non-polar covalent compounds.
rubric.description: They generally have low melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: State that their melting point or boiling point is generally low.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for another valid property of non-polar covalent compounds.
rubric.description: They generally do not conduct electricity; many are insoluble in water.
rubric.how: Give a valid property distinct from their low melting or boiling points.

modelAnswer: Non-polar covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They do not conduct electricity; many are insoluble in water and dissolve in non-polar solvents.

items.followUp: Why is the covalent bond in Cl₂ non-polar?

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for identifying why the two hydrogen atoms attract the bonding electrons equally.
rubric.description: The hydrogen atoms are identical and have the same electronegativity.
rubric.how: State that the atoms are identical or have equal electronegativity.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for explaining the resulting equal sharing or absence of poles.
rubric.description: The bonding pair is shared equally, so no positive or negative poles develop.
rubric.how: Explain that equal sharing prevents the formation of poles.

modelAnswer: The two hydrogen atoms are identical and have the same electronegativity.
They share the bonding pair equally, so no positive or negative poles develop in the H₂ molecule.

items.followUp: Explain how increasing external pressure affects the boiling point of a liquid.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for stating how external pressure changes the boiling point.
rubric.description: Increasing external pressure raises the boiling point, while decreasing it lowers the boiling point.
rubric.how: State the correct direction of change between external pressure and boiling point.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for explaining the condition at which a liquid boils.
rubric.description: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure becomes equal to the external pressure.
rubric.how: State that boiling occurs when vapour pressure equals external pressure.

modelAnswer: Increasing the external pressure raises the boiling point of a liquid; decreasing the pressure lowers it.
A liquid boils when its vapour pressure becomes equal to the external pressure.
